purpose: Corpus-hygiene repetition passes for a staged acquisition manifest, at two grains. Document mode (default) uses MinHash-LSH only to retrieve candidate cross-source near-duplicates, then exact-confirms every destructive edge against normalized shingle sets before it drops near-identical reposts/reprints the exact-hash guard misses. Passage mode (--passages) is the sub-document lens: Stage A clusters near-duplicate raw paragraphs (complete frequency-ordered Jaccard-prefix candidates confirmed by EXACT Jaccard), Stage B is a stdlib exact inverted-index scan that finds every contiguous verbatim span repeated at >= 2 locations regardless of what surrounds it. Passage mode is report-first and emits no verdict; spans are reported for consumer-side masking, never excised.
use_when: You have a staged impostor-corpus manifest and want to remove near-duplicate documents (syndicated reposts, lightly edited reprints, the same essay pulled from two sources) that the exact SHA-256 dedup does not catch.
You are merging acquisition output from multiple sources / directories and need cross-source dedup before the pool feeds voice-distance / General-Imposters baselines.

You need the SUB-document lens (--passages) — a passage repeated inside one document or across otherwise-distinct documents, which both the exact-hash guard and document-level near-dup are structurally blind to. Stage B's detection guarantee is arithmetic rather than thresholded — every verbatim repeated span of at least max(--span-shingle-k, --min-span-words) tokens is reported, exactly and deterministically.

You are staging a corpus for continued pretraining / fine-tuning and want a repeated-span inventory with per-occurrence provenance to drive loss masking or chunk-stream filtering on the training side.
do_not_use_when: You only need exact-duplicate removal — acquisition_core.content_hash_already_present already handles that inline during acquisition.

datasketch is not installed and you cannot add the optional acquisition dep (the pass raises a clear RuntimeError naming requirements-acquisition.txt). Stage B alone (--passages --stages b) runs stdlib-only.

You want to know whether a corpus is PROSE. That is check_corpus.py's question (non-prose contamination — CSS/HTML/code/tables spaCy would POS-tag as prose); this asks whether the prose is REPEATED. A corpus can be 100% clean prose and still carry one passage five times, so the two are orthogonal gates an operator may run on the same staged manifest; neither replaces the other.

The corpus is about to feed a duplicate-dependent set-level-diversity surface (corpus_novelty_audit, homogeneity_audit, distinct_diversity_audit, skeleton_overlap_audit, cross_doc_novelty_profile). Those measure signals that live IN the retained duplicates, so a passage-deduped pool destroys the measured object — they refuse a `passage_dedup`-marked manifest via pool_guard, and the fix is to feed them the PRE-dedup source manifest.
You want an excision / masking tool. Stage B never rewrites documents, and passage mode never rewrites the input manifest.

You need proof that every retained document is unique. Document mode's exact confirmation prevents candidate false positives from causing drops, but LSH candidate false negatives can leave true near-duplicates retained; this is an optional hygiene pass, not an exhaustive uniqueness certificate.

inputs.target: A JSONL acquisition manifest (inline `text` or a resolvable `text_path`/`path` per row).
optional: --checkpoint FILE to choose the exact-bound passage-mode checkpoint.
--resume to restore completed passage/document shards and stages from that checkpoint (or the automatic opaque temp checkpoint).

artifacts: A deduplicated JSONL manifest (dropped rows removed, all others preserved in order).

A DedupResult report (kept/dropped ids + near-duplicate clusters + threshold provenance), on stdout with --json. The report binds the datasketch package version, MinHash scheme and seed, normalization, ephemeral-rebuild-only index policy, candidate-pair count, and exact confirmation count.

Passage mode: a JSON report (stdout with --json, or --report-out FILE) carrying the Stage-A cluster / Stage-B span inventory with per-occurrence provenance, plus a mandatory `assumptions` params-and-limits block and a real ClaimLicense on the voice_coherence_acquisition surface.

Passage mode with --out MANIFEST --passage-dir DIR: a manifest_validator-clean passage-unit manifest (one row per kept passage, every inheritable source field including ai_status / privacy / consent_status copied verbatim, plus the `passage_dedup` marker) alongside one text file per passage. The export refuses entirely rather than inventing a missing ai_status or use, dropping an unreadable row, colliding filenames, nesting either output target inside the other, or publishing partial sidecars.

Passage mode SQLite shard checkpoints (automatic opaque temp path or --checkpoint) with flushed progress and exact-bound --resume. Corpus-derived shards live in a private mode-0700 directory / mode-0600 database; corrupt databases/payloads and invalid checkpoint paths refuse without a traceback.

compute.cost_note: Document mode uses MinHash-LSH for candidate retrieval and exact normalized shingle Jaccard for every union edge; datasketch pulls numpy/scipy. Candidate false negatives remain possible, while candidate false positives cannot authorize a drop. Passage Stage A uses complete frequency-ordered Jaccard prefix filtering with length/positional upper bounds, exact rational threshold arithmetic, and exact confirmation. Optional within the acquisition tier — lazy-imported, so base import stays clean. Stage B is pure stdlib but holds an O(corpus tokens) inverted index in one process. Passage CLI runs emit progress and transactionally checkpoint each passage/document shard; --resume restores exact-bound partial work.

examples.description: Report document-level near-duplicate clusters without rewriting the manifest
Drop document-level near-duplicates at a custom Jaccard threshold and write a new manifest
Run passage mode (both stages) and emit the JSON report on stdout
Run passage mode Stage B only (exact repeated-span scan) and write the span report to a file
Run passage mode and export a deduplicated passage-unit manifest plus one text file per passage
